      <title>Russian warship sinks in Benghazi after suspected Ukrainian drone attack</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya</link>
      <description><p>No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia</p><p>A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel.</p><p>The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/blast-russian-ship-suspected-drone-attack-benghazi-libya">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>California’s coastal communities on alert as biggest waves in years hit state</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state</link>
      <description><p>Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded</p><p>Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years.</p><p>Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10-18ft are expected, with local sets of 18-22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. Already, record-breaking rainfall affected San Fransisco on Wednesday, with heavy rain also causing 32,000 customers to lose power in Sacramento. Into this weekend, a further area of low pressure will bring considerable amounts of moisture for southern Oregon and northern California. By Sunday night, more than 100mm (4in) of rain is expected in places, with further snowfall for areas such as Donner Pass across the northern Sierra Nevada mountains.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/20/california-coastal-communities-alert-big-waves-hit-state">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe</link>
      <description><p>The trees, intended for an unnamed buyer in Georgia, were reportedly dug up without the necessary permits</p><p>Environmentalists in South Africa are racing to replant five centuries-old baobabs after the 20-tonne trees were dug up by an exporter, who tried to ship them thousands of miles to Georgia.</p><p>The baobabs arrived at a reserve in Timbavati, in north-eastern South Africa, on Wednesday, where they will be replanted and supported by cables to help them recover. The trees had been stranded at a warehouse in Durban since July, when they were intercepted by authorities who said they had been moved without the necessary permissions.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/19/baobab-five-trees-south-africa-dug-up-export-blocked-georgia-aoe">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/nov/19/women-girls-rights-rape-sexual-violence-africa-marriage-unfpa</link>
      <description><p>Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds</p><p>One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.</p><p>In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament.       <description><p>New research finds that the British-led Cobre Mining Company helped industrialise Manchester via copper deposits and enslaved African people</p><p>• <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/ng-interactive/2026/sep/16/slave-trade-wealth-britain-financial-system-bank-of-england-enslaved-africans">Slave-trade wealth was embedded in Britain’s financial system, research finds</a></p><p>British businesses run by long-serving directors of the Bank of England profited from “brutal” enslavement in Cuba for decades after slavery’s abolition in the British empire, according to research.</p><p>Men and boys were enslaved in prison conditions at the El Cobre copper ore mine near Santiago de Cuba, which supplied British firms during the Industrial Revolution, the historian Chris Evans has found.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/news/2026/nov/22/bank-of-england-directors-illegally-profited-enslavement-cuba">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers</link>
      <description><p>Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner</p><p>The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/race-to-be-next-un-secretary-general-exposes-divisions-among-world-powers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Australia urged to wean off imported fossil fuels amid global supply shocks</title>

      <description><p>Grattan Institute report calls on government to seize opportunity to cap diesel tax credits, introduce EV subsidies for less wealthy and build ‘clean’ refineries</p><ul><li><p>Get our <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/email-newsletters?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily political email</a>, <a href="https://app.adjust.com/w4u7jx3">free app</a> or <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/series/full-story?CMP=cvau_sfl">daily news podcast</a></p></li></ul><p>Capping lucrative diesel tax handouts to big business, building new “clean” refineries and targeting electric vehicle subsidies to less wealthy people could save Australians thousands of dollars in fuel per year, according to a major new report calling on the government to reduce reliance on imported fossil fuels.</p><p>The Grattan Institute has warned Australia imports too much of its fuel and that the country must brace for more global supply shocks – like those from the war in Iran. Under a plan already attracting criticism from business groups, Grattan urged diesel handouts to mining and primary industries be curbed in favour of incentives for electric trucks and a huge expansion of the EV charging network.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/nov/23/australia-urged-to-wean-off-imported-fossil-fuels-amid-global-supply-shocks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>US intelligence chief says he trusts Trump’s description of Putin as ‘my friend’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend</link>
      <description><p>Jay Clayton was pressed on Trump’s characterization of Putin during media appearances on Sunday</p><p>Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/video/2026/nov/19/trump-greets-putin-before-holding-talks-at-apec-summit-video">their recent meeting</a> in China.</p><p>Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. After a backlash at home and aboard, Trump doubled down on Saturday and <a href="https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117656427563362319">posted a photo of himself and Putin </a>shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/intelligence-chief-jay-clayton-trump-putin-my-friend">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected</link>
      <description><p>EU, UK and some of developing world object to main text that ‘failed to meet the moment’ and did not mention fossil fuels</p><p>The EU, the UK and allies in the developing world rejected what they called an unacceptable deal on the future of the climate, which failed even to mention fossil fuels, in a dramatic finish to the Cop31 UN talks in Turkey.</p><p>The proposed deal “failed to meet the moment”, said Ireland’s environment minister, Darragh O’Brien, speaking for the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required. [It] does not even mention fossil fuels.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/22/cop31-climate-talks-set-to-end-in-deep-division-as-key-deal-rejected">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long</p><p>British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products.</p><p>The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/03/deal-finalised-remove-brexit-checks-food-animal-products">benefit Britain’s food exporters</a> and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/22/uk-eu-food-sps-deal-brexit-checks">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Kraftwerk Berlin, part of same development as techno club Tresor, transformed into ‘war room’ for arms firm event</p><p>With their cavernous post-industrial venues, teeth-grinding four-by-four beats and bouncers that look like Blade Runner extras, Berlin’s nightclubs trade on a reputation for bleakness.       <title>Europe is entering a ‘supercycle’ of national elections. Their outcomes could shake the EU’s foundations</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/europe-elections-supercycle-could-shake-eu-foundations</link>
      <description><p>As nationalist, Eurosceptic parties surge in four of the bloc’s biggest member states, the coming year’s polls could test its resilience like never before</p><p>In late 1998, Tony Blair was prime minister of Britain, Lionel Jospin was prime minister of France, and Gerhard Schröder had just been elected chancellor of Germany. The EU had 15 member states and pro-European, centre-left parties were in power – either alone or in coalitions – in all but two of them.</p><p>Brisk economic growth was lifting living standards. Eastward enlargement was under way. In Washington, Bill Clinton was pursuing the same brand of “third way” centrism as a middle path between free-market capitalism and traditional socialism. The EU felt like it had the tide of history behind it.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/22/europe-elections-supercycle-could-shake-eu-foundations">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack</p><p>Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/september11">9/11</a>.</p><p>Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/live/2026/nov/13/microsoft-outage-down-today-live-update-outlook-teams-365-when-fixed-latest-status-cause-news">global Microsoft outage</a>. She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/22/hacks-ai-internet-outages-airlines-banks-microsoft-apple">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Two weeks after Democrats flipped Congress, conservative outlets are having conversations on whether to distance themselves from Trump or double down on Maga</p><p>As a so-called “blue wave” crashed across the country on the night of 3 November, conservative hosts and commentators on Fox News <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/04/trump-blames-fox-news-republican-losses">displayed an almost virtuosic ability to avoid directly blaming Donald Trump</a> for the Republican party’s defeat, instead pinning the blame on impertinent voters who didn’t grasp the strength of the economy.</p><p>“In some sense, Mr Trump was too successful in the first year and didn’t sell it enough in the second year,” said Larry Kudlow, a Fox Business Network host who served as the president’s director of the National Economic Council during his first administration.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/22/conservative-media-trump-midterm-elections-results">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The Nasdaq lost trillions in value, with the AI startup’s IPO failing to buoy it as investors question huge sums being poured into AI buildout</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/who-are-anthropic-founders">Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?</a></p></li></ul><p>As Anthropic’s stock dropped during its second day of trading, the wider stock market dipped with it. The Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&amp;P 500 closed in correction territory.</p><p>Anthropic’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/19/anthropic-public-trading-ipo">record-breaking IPO</a> failed to stem a global sell-off in AI-linked companies, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq erased some <a href="https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/anthropics-ipo-bust-punctuates-4-trillion-ai-wipeout-on-wall-street-f1f1ec90?mod=WSJ_home_mediumtopper_pos_1">$4tn in market value</a> this week, according to the Wall Street Journal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/2026/nov/20/global-stock-markets-slump-anthropic-ipo-ai-sell-off">Continue reading...</a></description>

The latest information, news and events in France, Europe and around the world.</description><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:10:28 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>French right backs Macron's plan to put public spending limits in Constitution</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261122-french-right-backs-macron-s-plan-to-put-public-spending-limits-in-constitution</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron is reportedly considering a constitutional reform to curb public deficits, with right-wing parties and the far-right National Rally signalling their willingness to support the move. The proposal could bring MPs and senators together for a vote as early as January, just months before the 2027 presidential election.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4bea9e76-e66c-11f1-b8f3-f96315fbf1b4</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 18:09:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/445a5ffc-e662-11f1-8900-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/000-36LK6NK-1.jpg">AFP - STEPHANIE LECOCQ</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Students and unions unite for sixth weekend of protests across France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-students-and-unions-unite-for-sixth-weekend-of-protests-across-france</link><description>
Thousands of demonstrators took to the streets across France on Saturday for a sixth consecutive weekend of protests against rising living costs, deteriorating public services and growing inequality. The movement, which began with student demonstrations in September, has since broadened into a nationwide campaign and inspired similar rallies elsewhere in Europe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7ad79414-e5c2-11f1-8bc6-7d93519529c2</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:43:57 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/1a778cb4-e5b3-11f1-a8b6-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88M7VC.jpg">AFP - GUILLAUME SALIGOT</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French court finds racism played role in police beating of black music producer</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-french-court-finds-racism-played-role-in-police-beating-of-black-music-producer</link><description>
A French court has handed down prison sentences to three police officers for the violent assault of black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris in 2020, ruling that racism was an aggravating factor in a case that sparked nationwide outrage over police brutality and racial discrimination.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">eadc87ac-e58a-11f1-b7fe-efd3e07e368d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:41:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/17c071ac-e4f5-11f1-9df3-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-20T101436Z-2082553690-RC2LROA9VG3U-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-JUSTICE-ZECLER.jpg">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>National Assembly backs greater legal protection for police using firearms</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-national-assembly-backs-greater-legal-protection-for-police-using-firearms</link><description>
France's parliament has approved legislation giving police officers greater legal protection when using their firearms, prompting fierce criticism from rights groups who warn it could make it harder to investigate alleged police brutality. The government insists the measure is needed to protect officers carrying out increasingly demanding duties.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a15be40c-e589-11f1-9ce2-a7af964aafae</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:44:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/07ce511e-d53d-11f1-ab78-1beafce15fea/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-31T142906Z-217842348-RC2CEOAPZ05N-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Nicolas Economou</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Former PM de Villepin launches 2027 presidential bid with warning to far right</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-former-pm-de-villepin-launches-20207-presidential-bid-with-warning-to-far-right</link><description>
Former French prime minister Dominique de Villepin has announced his candidacy for the 2027 presidential election, promising to restore France's international influence, tackle growing inequality and challenge the rise of the far right. The veteran conservative also delivered a blistering assessment of President Emmanuel Macron's leadership, accusing him of allowing the country's political and social divisions to deepen.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf6f11fc-e589-11f1-b2ac-0d673b4c7b00</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 12:02:37 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bedb7fd4-e4ed-11f1-9e70-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324386665816.jpg">AP Photo/Aurelien Morissard - Aurelien Morissard</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France must change or 'risk losing' overseas territories, former PM tells RFI</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261121-france-must-change-or-risk-losing-overseas-territories-former-pm-tells-rfi-manuel-valls</link><description>
France's territories outside Europe are a major strategic asset, giving it a foothold on five continents and in three oceans. Yet Paris has long been accused of neglecting the nearly 3 million people living outside mainland France, who face deep economic and social inequalities. With calls for independence growing, former prime minister Manuel Valls warns that France risks losing its overseas territories unless it radically changes its relationship with them.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c2eb5f78-e343-11f1-ac1e-392da9561c55</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 08:31:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/5b00a846-f5b5-11ef-a324-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_36YE3UC.jpg">© AFP - DELPHINE MAYEUR </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French Greens candidate gives hard-left Mélenchon a boost in presidential race</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-french-greens-candidate-gives-hard-left-melenchon-a-boost-in-presidential-race</link><description>
French hard-left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon has said an alliance with the Greens "should be possible", after the head of the Greens tentatively agreed to back him, angering moderates on the centre-left. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">40b0fb0e-e4dc-11f1-a123-31d05317ef57</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:04:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/803220b8-e4e7-11f1-a2f9-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-19T085824Z-1059669313-RC2NXNA8BALJ-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-POLITICS-GREENS.jpg">© REUTERS - Tom Nicholson </source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Depardieu and Houellebecq accused of gang rape on French film set</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261120-depardieu-and-houellebecq-accused-of-gang-rape-on-french-film-set</link><description>
Paris prosecutors have opened an investigation after an actress filed a complaint alleging that she was raped by a group including actor Gérard Depardieu and high-profile French author Michel Houellebecq on the set of the film Thalasso in 2018.

      <title>Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at ­Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for ­denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again.</p><p>Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s&nbsp;Premier League history.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/liverpool-manchester-united-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>McBurnie’s added-time double snatches win for Hull to shock 10-man Brighton</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>Amid the talk of Brighton being surprise title contenders this season, these are perhaps the afternoons which show the margin that still exists, and how the Premier League can provide the most punishing of wake-up calls at any moment.</p><p>Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. But for all the statement victories and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/brighton-rocking-premier-league-elite-title-challenge">the headline-grabbing moments</a>, these games are the ones which can trip you up the most.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/hull-brighton-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/manchester-city-tottenham-wsl-match-report</link>
      <description><p>This most unpredictable and evenly contested Women’s Super League campaign took another unexpected twist as Manchester City missed the chance to return to the top of the table as they suffered a second successive defeat, by virtue of a terrific performance from a Tottenham side who moved within three points of the European places.</p><p>The shock result came just 24 hours after City’s title rivals Chelsea had dropped points at Liverpool.       <description><p></p><p>Todd Cantwell’s penalty earned Blackburn a 2-2 draw at Burnley in their first match since <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/17/blackburn-rovers-tony-mowbray-steps-down-due-to-health-issues">Tony Mowbray stepped back</a> because of health issues.</p><p>In a gripping, physical East Lancashire derby, the home side led twice, through Largie Ramazani’s rising first-half drive and Jaydon Banel’s steered finish after the break.       <title>Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/19/thomas-frank-crystal-palace-premier-league">that the new manager</a> bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row.</p><p>Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/coventry-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

This passive draw was met with boos from the home fans.</p><p>Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence. They had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/manchester-city-fulham-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out</link>
      <description><p>Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement</p><p>César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like <em>not</em> being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot.</p><p>It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/22/cesar-azpilicueta-at-chelsea-a-draw-was-a-catastrophe-if-you-cant-perform-youre-out">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england</link>
      <description><p>The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player</p><p>Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.</p><p>He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor &amp; Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/20/dele-alli-tottenham-mk-dons-england">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon.</p><p>It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/21/chelsea-leeds-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom" xmlns:media="http://search.yahoo.com/mrss/" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><language>fr</language><title><![CDATA[France 24 - Infos, news & actualités - L'information internationale en direct]]></title><description>France 24 décrypte l’actualité internationale, politique, l’économie, l’environnement, la culture, le sport, en France et à l’international avec analyses, des interviews, des reportages exclusifs, des magazines et des documentaires.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:53:08 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/fr/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Journal de l'Afrique</category><title>Elections générales en RD Congo, la Symocel doute de la possibilité de tenir les délais</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/journal-de-l-afrique/20261122-elections-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rales-en-rd-congo-la-symocel-doute-de-la-possibilit%C3%A9-de-tenir-les-d%C3%A9lais</link><description>
En RD Congo, se dirige-t-on vers un report des élections générales ? Les scrutins sont prévus en décembre 2028. Dans un rapport publié en novembre, la Symocel, l’une des missions d’observation électorale, doute de la possibilité de tenir ce délai...
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e8ac38-e6bc-11f1-b05d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/WB299310-O-01-20261122-01.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/78e8ac38-e6bc-11f1-b05d-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/WB299310-O-01-20261122-01.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">af117e7e-e6bd-11f1-b884-73184c4a7611</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:42:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Kalidou SY</dc:creator></item><item><category>Afrique</category><title>Libye : deux navires attaqués par des drones maritimes, dont un bateau russe</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20261122-libye-drones-maritimes-attaqu%C3%A9-deux-navires-bateau-russe-guerre</link><description>
Un incendie s'est déclaré dimanche après une explosion à bord d'un navire russe dans la base navale de Benghazi, en Libye. Le ministère de la Santé des autorités de l'Est a indiqué que le bateau avait été "ciblé par des drones maritimes". Dans la soirée, un deuxième bateau, dont le pavillon n'a pas été communiqué, a été attaqué dans le même port.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">8156d5f6-e6b8-11f1-a6fb-6fc2f3d2d784</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 21:05:53 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/659e3cc8-e6a9-11f1-ae55-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26326649718247.jpg">© AP via Vanto satellite image</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Philippe Sands : "l'arrêt de la CIJ fait partie des moments-clés qui changent l'Histoire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-philippe-sands-l-arr%C3%AAt-de-la-cij-fait-partie-des-moments-cl%C3%A9s-qui-changent-l-histoire</link><description>
La Cour Internationale de Justice a reconnu un génocide commis par la Birmanie à l'encontre de la minorité musulmane des Rohingya. La CIJ demande à ce que les réfugiés rohingya, pour la plupart entassés dans des camps au Bangladesh, puissent revenir en Birmanie et être indemnisés. L'avocat franco-britannique Philippe Sands, l'un des avocats qui ont représenté la Gambie contre la Birmanie devant la CIJ, était l'Invité d'Au Cœur de l'Info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/224f14cc-e6b0-11f1-8ccf-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-204153-205702-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">a96fd46c-e6b7-11f1-93d6-fb174a76721d</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:59:51 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Caroline Toby : "sans vidéosurveillance, Michel Zecler aurait été victime d'une erreur judiciaire"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261122-caroline-toby-sans-vid%C3%A9osurveillance-michel-zecler-aurait-%C3%A9t%C3%A9-victime-d-une-erreur-judiciaire</link><description>
Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences; or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtent à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-choose-france-entreprises-fran%C3%A7aises-pr%C3%AAtent-investir-42-5-milliards-euros-emmanuel-macron-%C3%A9conomie-investissements-projet</link><description>
Les entreprises tricolores projettent d'investir 42,5 milliards d'euros en France lors du sommet Choose France qui se déroulera lundi, a détaillé l'Élysée dimanche soir. Malgré une situation économique compliquée dans le pays, plus de 200 projets industriels français seront mis à l'honneur.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">19c1b856-e6af-11f1-a7d0-d531a8636e90</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 19:58:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0b2fc994-e6ab-11f1-9ffc-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26152618587040.jpg">© Gonzalo Fuentes, Pool Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>La COP31 s'achève sur un échec, l'UE rejette la proposition d'accord final</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-la-cop31-s-ach%C3%A8ve-sur-un-%C3%A9chec-l-ue-rejette-la-proposition-d-accord-final</link><description>
La COP31 ​se dirigeait dimanche 22 novembre vers un échec et le rejet par une majorité de pays du texte de conclusion présenté par la Turquie et l'Australie, qui pilotaient les négociations, un compromis ​jugé bien trop timoré par nombre de pays participants.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/010851ae-e686-11f1-a89c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-140157-141003-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/010851ae-e686-11f1-a89c-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-140157-141003-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">062803aa-e686-11f1-a08e-cf88b7f8ff51</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:41:59 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Corée du Sud : démission du ministre de l'Éducation après un scandale de triche à l'IA</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cor%C3%A9e-du-sud-d%C3%A9mission-du-ministre-de-l-%C3%A9ducation-apr%C3%A8s-un-scandale-de-triche-%C3%A0-l-ia</link><description>
Le ministre de l'Éducation sud-coréen a démissionné dimanche 22 novembre, emporté par un scandale de triche à l'intelligence artificielle qui a semé le doute quant à la bonne tenue des sacro-saints examens d'entrée à l'université.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9a4414ba-e68c-11f1-bf46-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141343-141531-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/9a4414ba-e68c-11f1-bf46-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141343-141531-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">9f80b302-e68c-11f1-892b-a39073915c40</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:41:05 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Ukraine : au moins deux morts après une frappe de drone russe contre un immeuble résidentiel</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-ukraine-au-moins-deux-morts-apr%C3%A8s-une-frappe-de-drone-russe-contre-un-immeuble-r%C3%A9sidentiel</link><description>
Au ​moins deux personnes ont été tuées et une ​dizaine d'autres pourraient encore se trouver piégées sous les décombres d'un immeuble résidentiel frappé par un drone russe ​ce dimanche ‌22 novembre matin dans l'oblast de Kiev, ⁠ont déclaré le président Volodymyr Zelensky et des responsables locaux.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe6cd88-e68d-11f1-abe4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-150424-150600-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/abe6cd88-e68d-11f1-abe4-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-150424-150600-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b0fc8768-e68d-11f1-880f-97845bc94794</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:39:36 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>De la Seine-Saint-Denis à la Nasa, retour sur le parcours d'Allan Petre</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-de-la-seine-saint-denis-%C3%A0-la-nasa-retour-sur-le-parcours-d-allan-petre</link><description>
L'ingénieur aérospatial Allan Petre a intégré la Nasa a 24 ans, ce qui fait de lui l'un des plus jeunes Français à y parvenir. Il publie "Astro Allan", une bande-dessinée retraçant son parcours.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7c6acbcc-e68d-11f1-82fb-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141656-142707-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7c6acbcc-e68d-11f1-82fb-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-141656-142707-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">81e42472-e68d-11f1-bdc9-97845bc94794</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:38:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Climat : la COP31 échoue devant la division des pays sur les énergies fossiles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-climat-la-cop31-%C3%A9choue-devant-la-division-des-pays-sur-les-%C3%A9nergies-fossiles</link><description>
La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec ce dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b2b3502-e68e-11f1-ba46-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160141-160331-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b2b3502-e68e-11f1-ba46-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160141-160331-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3039e6c4-e68e-11f1-bd13-c3178e8c146c</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:37:45 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 à Antalya : pas d'accord en vue ?</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-pas-d-accord-en-vue</link><description>
La COP31 à Antalya est déjà la COP la plus longue de l’histoire, avec 44 heures de prolongations. Les négociations s’enlisent sur les énergies fossiles. Nous en parlons avec notre correspondante Jenna Le Bras.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a9cca28-e68f-11f1-80c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-120103-120442-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a9cca28-e68f-11f1-80c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-120103-120442-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7fc9d680-e68f-11f1-889c-a757f882d559</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:35:32 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 à Antalya : la plus longue COP de l'histoire s'achève sur un échec</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-la-plus-longue-cop-de-l-histoire-s-ach%C3%A8ve-sur-un-%C3%A9chec</link><description>
La COP31, la plus longue conférence de l'ONU sur le climat de l'histoire, s'est terminée sur un échec dimanche 22 novembre à Antalya, en Turquie, après le rejet par l'Union européenne et d'autres pays d'un projet de décision finale omettant les énergies fossiles. "On ressent de la déception et beaucoup de colère, parce que ce scénario aurait pu être évité", rapporte notre invitée Marine Pouget, responsable de la gouvernance internationale sur le climat au sein du Réseau Action Climat.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a88dc460-e68e-11f1-8b4d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160332-160953-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a88dc460-e68e-11f1-8b4d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-160332-160953-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ad688a2e-e68e-11f1-92ab-cdddf46835ec</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:35:25 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Échec de la COP31 à Antalya : "Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-%C3%A9chec-de-la-cop31-%C3%A0-antalya-nous-sommes-pass%C3%A9s-%C3%A0-c%C3%B4t%C3%A9-d-une-opportunit%C3%A9</link><description>
"Nous sommes passés à côté d'une opportunité", a reconnu le président de la COP après de très longues négociations. La COP31 à Antalya se termine donc sur un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre invitée Charlotte Chaussat, cofondatrice de la Coordination Climat. "Cette COP se passait dans un climat compliqué", rappelle-t-elle.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c43d5b72-e665-11f1-a6c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-22T095903Z-917320092-RC2XSOA2A529-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c43d5b72-e665-11f1-a6c8-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-22T095903Z-917320092-RC2XSOA2A529-RTRMADP-3-CLIMATE-COP31.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">51a71434-e68f-11f1-a222-df3693cae406</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:34:17 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>COP31 : décryptage après son échec malgré 44 heures de prolongations</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-cop31-d%C3%A9cryptage-apr%C3%A8s-son-%C3%A9chec-malgr%C3%A9-44-heures-de-prolongations</link><description>
La COP31 à Antalya se solde par un échec. Nous en parlons avec notre chroniqueuse Anne Corpet. "À la COP, les décisions se prennent par consensus : il faut l'unanimité. Le constat, c’est que l’alliance des pays hostiles à toute avancée a été plus forte que celle de ceux qui souhaitent avancer sur le plan climatique", explique-t-elle.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48155c68-e690-11f1-ab2c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-170326-170857-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/48155c68-e690-11f1-ab2c-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-170326-170857-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">4d3f6274-e690-11f1-84d0-cff2360bfc82</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:30:55 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France : un "marché de Noël d'autrefois" à Villeneuve d'Ascq</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-france-un-march%C3%A9-de-no%C3%ABl-d-autrefois-%C3%A0-villeneuve-d-ascq</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">fb9ec900-e680-11f1-8380-d59eaff5322f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 14:28:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/83540fda-e696-11f1-ba48-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26324374289119.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, Pool AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Afrique</category><title>Des frappes de drones imputées à l'Éthiopie ciblent la capitale soudanaise</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/afrique/20261122-des-frappes-de-drones-imput%C3%A9es-%C3%A0-l-%C3%A9thiopie-touchent-des-habitations-%C3%A0-khartoum</link><description>
Des habitations et un bâtiment des Nations unies ont été touchés, dimanche, par des frappes de drones à Khartoum, au Soudan. Une source proche de l'armée a affirmé que l'Éthiopie voisine pourrait être responsable. Depuis mars 2025, la capitale soudanaise a été reprise par l'armée aux paramilitaires des Forces de soutien rapide (FSR).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccc06aae-e675-11f1-9926-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/f05172441673b3dfece3c83ad6495393e2fb4735.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccc06aae-e675-11f1-9926-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/f05172441673b3dfece3c83ad6495393e2fb4735.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cd86ee04-e675-11f1-8d93-2bff2a2123cb</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 13:08:25 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ccc06aae-e675-11f1-9926-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/f05172441673b3dfece3c83ad6495393e2fb4735.jpg">© Ebrahim Hamid, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France : cinquantenaire de la mort d’André Malraux ce lundi</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/vid%C3%A9o/20261122-france-cinquantenaire-de-la-mort-d-andr%C3%A9-malraux-ce-lundi</link><description>

Un ancien chef de la police italienne, qui faisait l'objet d'une enquête en lien avec l'assassinat en 1992 du juge antimafia Paolo Borsellino, a été retrouvé mort, rapporte la presse italienne samedi 21 novembre.
 
Gianni De Gennaro, âgé de 78 ans, se serait donné la mort par arme à feu alors qu'il se trouvait seul dans sa maison de campagne en Toscane, indiquent les médias italiens.
 
Selon la Repubblica, son corps a été retrouvé samedi matin à l'aube, après que ses proches, inquiets de ne pas avoir de nouvelles depuis la veille au soir, aient donné l'alarme.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/aa4c4418-e669-11f1-8a47-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-110351-110536-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/aa4c4418-e669-11f1-8a47-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-110351-110536-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">af49f136-e669-11f1-8552-b1adb80e046f</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 12:37:35 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Asie-Pacifique</category><title>Sommet tripartite de Shenzhen, COP 31 et gronde sociale en France : la semaine en images</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/asie-pacifique/20261122-sommet-tripartite-de-shenzhen-cop-31-et-gronde-sociale-en-france-la-semaine-en-images</link><description>

            <title><![CDATA[« Voir sa mère dans la pauvreté et être incapable de l'aider, c'est très dur », pourquoi ces pêcheurs veulent tous quitter le Sénégal]]></title>
            <description><![CDATA[De jeunes pêcheurs de Yenne Todd, âgés de 18 à 22 ans, ne cachent ni leur désarroi ni leur envie de partir. Confrontés à des conditions de vie difficiles et à l'absence de perspectives économiques, ils disent ne plus entrevoir leur avenir au Sénégal. Pour eux, rejoindre l'Europe, même au péril de leur vie, apparaît comme la seule alternative pour sortir de la précarité et d'aider leurs parents.]]></description>

            <description><![CDATA[Les abus sexuels commis sur des enfants dans des écoles religieuses au Bangladesh ont mis en lumière les souffrances endurées par les victimes et leurs familles. Un père, Khairul Bashar, a exprimé sa douleur et sa colère face aux sévices subis par son fils : "je ne peux supporter ce qui est arrivé à mon fils et je ferai en sorte que le coupable soit traduit en justice."]]></description>

Le producteur Michel Zecler avait été passé à tabac en 2020 par trois policiers dans l'entrée de son studio d'enregistrement à Paris. Les policiers avaient établi un faux procès-verbal l'accusant de violences; or les images de vidéosurveillance avaient invalidé leur version. Les policiers viennent d'être condamnés à de la prison ferme, avec interdiction d'exercer leur métier. Le caractère raciste de ces violences a aussi été reconnu. Interview de Caroline Toby, avocate de Michel Zecler.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/912ca82c-e6ac-11f1-a33d-ebb478925cf0/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261122-201335-202201-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">88d84f80-e6b3-11f1-a209-c955afc4fa26</guid><pubDate>Sun, 22 Nov 2026 20:30:18 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Choose France : les entreprises françaises prêtent à investir 42,5 milliards d'euros</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261122-choose-france-entreprises-fran%C3%A7aises-pr%C3%AAtent-investir-42-5-milliards-euros-emmanuel-macron-%C3%A9conomie-investissements-projet</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7c4cc2e-e5e5-11f1-a66f-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88T7BJ.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7c4cc2e-e5e5-11f1-a66f-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88T7BJ.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">18084e40-e573-11f1-9a90-2dc31e39031d</guid><pubDate>Sat, 21 Nov 2026 06:16:30 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/c7c4cc2e-e5e5-11f1-a66f-6b451f569414/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D88T7BJ.jpg">© Romain Perrocheau, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Procès Zecler : les trois policiers condamnés à des peines de un à deux ans de prison ferme</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-proc%C3%A8s-zecler-les-trois-policiers-condamn%C3%A9s-%C3%A0-des-peines-de-un-%C3%A0-deux-ans-de-prison-ferme</link><description>

</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">844245cc-e52b-11f1-ab61-a5c9daa303ca</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 21:54:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0daede70-e445-11f1-aa9e-13439ca2fe89/w:1024/p:16x9/6eafad5bb555456f4505bd99516b8a173e5764e7.jpg">© Benoit PEYRUCQ / AFP/Archives</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Au cœur de l’info, l’invité</category><title>Johann Chapoutot : "la dédiabolisation du RN est véritablement un mythe"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/au-c%C5%93ur-de-l-info-l-invit%C3%A9/20261120-johann-chapoutot-la-d%C3%A9diabolisation-du-rn-est-v%C3%A9ritablement-un-mythe</link><description>
A 5 mois de la présidentielle en France, le RN domine toujours dans les sondages. Longtemps considéré comme anti républicain, infréquentable, il est désormais aux portes du pouvoir. Comment comprendre cette progression? Quelle est la responsabilité de la classe politique dans cette évolution? Quelles conséquences sur notre démocratie? Johann Chapoutot, Professeur d'Histoire contemporaine, auteur de "La bascule, Allemagne 1933" (éditions Gallimard), était l'Invité d'Au Coeur de l'Info. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/20054536-e522-11f1-9d9f-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/FR-20261120-200854-202823-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">141cd51a-e525-11f1-8891-754dc11be848</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 20:58:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Achren VERDIAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Police : la loi sur la présomption de légitime défense définitivement adoptée par le Parlement</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-police-la-loi-sur-la-pr%C3%A9somption-de-l%C3%A9gitime-d%C3%A9fense-d%C3%A9finitivement-adopt%C3%A9e-par-le-parlement</link><description>
Vivement combattue dans la rue par ses opposants qui l'assimilent à un "permis de tuer", l'instauration d'une présomption d'usage légal des armes par les forces de l'ordre a été définitivement adoptée au Parlement vendredi soir, à la veille d'une nouvelle journée de mobilisation sociale.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ec88460c-e514-11f1-8bce-43bc8e8d3f8d</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 19:02:24 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/84d2817a-e524-11f1-9187-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C8TV3VK.jpg">© Geoffroy van der Hasselt, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fuites au ministère de l'Intérieur : comment le RN a progressivement séduit les hauts fonctionnaires</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-fuites-au-minist%C3%A8re-de-l-int%C3%A9rieur-comment-le-rn-a-progressivement-s%C3%A9duit-les-hauts-fonctionnaires</link><description>
Le parquet de Paris soupçonne l'ancien secrétaire général de Beauvau et actuel préfet du Loiret et de la région Centre-Val de Loire, Hugues Moutouh, d'avoir informé le Rassemblement national sur des enquêtes judiciaires visant le parti. La sécheresse s'installe durablement en Outre-mer. Le manque d'eau fragilise les cultures et menace les récoltes aux Antilles et à La Réunion. La situation est également très préoccupante en Guyane, où le niveau du fleuve continue de baisser.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d5ba9aa2-e4f5-11f1-a177-e56ab3dc0809/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-e00d5d0f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">668bbe98-e4ca-11f1-b006-117a06c45e07</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 15:36:16 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator></dc:creator></item><item><category>ActuElles</category><title>Les féminicides, la partie émergée du contrôle coercitif</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/%C3%A9missions/actuelles/20261120-les-f%C3%A9minicides-la-partie-%C3%A9merg%C3%A9e-du-contr%C3%B4le-coercitif</link><description>
Les féminicides font aussi des victimes invisibles : les proches des femmes assassinées, confrontées à un deuil impossible et à des embûches judiciaires. Dans 75 % des cas, le féminicide survient sans violences physiques préalables, mais au terme d'une période de contrôle coercitif :  une prison invisible faite d'emprise et de violences psychologiques, explique l'historienne Christelle Taraud, qui décrit des victimes "zombifiées" par leur tortionnaire.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/804fd37e-e4e7-11f1-94db-1bac47ab2f5d/w:1024/p:16x9/actuelles-4.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">012b0ea0-e4e8-11f1-954f-b12e286687bf</guid><pubDate>Fri, 20 Nov 2026 14:46:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Laure MANENT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Gérard Depardieu et Michel Houellebecq accusés de viol en réunion et d'agressions sexuelles</title><link>https://www.france24.com/fr/france/20261120-g%C3%A9rard-depardieu-et-michel-houellebecq-accus%C3%A9s-de-viol-en-r%C3%A9union-et-d-agressions-sexuelles</link><description>
